item.title: ‘If they lose today…’: Berbatov makes bleak Carrick/Man Utd admission just before Como clash
item.description: ‘If they lose today…’: Berbatov makes bleak Carrick/Man Utd admission just before Como clash Manchester United icon Dimitar Berbatov has categorised this evening’s clash between Manchester United and Como as a must-win game for Michael Carrick. The two sides are currently undergoing their final preparations ahead of kick-off before taking to the pitch for matchday three in the Champions League. How United have fared as of late Should United manage to take all three points from the encounter, it would mark their first win since September 10, when they overturned Azerbaijan outfit Sabah at Old Trafford in their UCL opener. A bigger concern, however, is that they have failed to win in the Premier League since August, with their only victory coming against newly-promoted outfit Ipswich Town at home. Last time out in Europe, they slumped to a 2-0 defeat away to Atletico Madrid, during which they had only a few clear-cut chances to get back into the tie after the hosts’ 53-second opener. Carrick’s injury woes & Berbatov’s pre-match admission Carrick is navigating a severely depleted squad in Italy tonight, as he is without the likes of Ayden Heaven, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez and Marcus Rashford. Patrick Dorgu, Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte are more long-term absentees due to injury, while Leny Yoro misses out through suspension after being shown a controversial red card at the Metropolitano. “If they lose today, the pressure will be even more. They need the win today no matter what. I don’t care how. Long ball, direct ball, possession — just get the win because the pressure will get less after the game,” said former striker Berbatov on TNT Sports. After the full-time whistle is blown later this evening, United will swiftly turn their attention to Sunday’s meeting with Bournemouth in M16. item.title: Quinshon Judkins Returning To Fantasy Football Lineups In Week 7 Will Impact Dylan Sampson And Jaleel McLaughlin
item.description: Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins (10) carries the ball against the Carolina Panthers during the first quarter at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After missing Week 6 with an ankle injury, Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken is optimistic that running back Quinshon Judkins will be able to return to action in Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans. Last week, Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime split the backfield in his absence. Head coach Todd Monken "is optimistic" that Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will play Sunday against the Titans. Via @DanielOyefusi pic.twitter.com/KiO9U6itVj - RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 21, 2026 Fantasy Impact RB Quinshon Judkins, Cleveland Browns If Judkins returns and is fully healthy, we expect him to step right back into his near bell-cow RB1 role. He can go right back into your starting lineups in a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. While the Titans haven't been terrible against the run, their game scripts often lead to opposing running backs getting a ton of work late in games. We expect that to be the case in this game, with the Browns being better than many people expected. Their defense is solid, and their offense has exceeded their extremely low expectations. We know Judkins will lead the backfield if he's cleared to play. However, it could get tricky when it comes to figuring out who could be the second option in the backfield. RB Dylan Sampson, Cleveland Browns Sampson had his 21-day practice window opened last week, but he wasn't able to return to action in Week 6. He will get his next chance to get on the field in Week 7. If Sampson returns to action and Judkins is active, he would likely fall into his change-of-pace and pass-catching role. He would not be startable in his first game back in this role. If he is active and Judkins isn't, then Sampson gets very interesting. Because of his pass-catching ability, he could step into a near bell-cow role. We would start him if he's in and Judkins is out. RB Jaleel McLaughlin, Cleveland Browns With Judkins back, McLaughlin would be relegated to the change-of-pace role. As we just said, Sampson could be back too, though. Sampson would make McLaughlin redundant and probably take any opportunities he might have seen. If either Judkins or Sampson plays, McLaughlin can be sent to waivers, especially if Sampson is activated. RB Audric Estime, Cleveland Browns Judkins returning would make Estime completely useless. Estime's only real purpose is to be used at the goal line for the smaller McLaughlin. That role goes away if Judkins is back. If only Sampson returns, Estime would have a chance to fall into the end zone again this week. He will likely be sent back to the practice squad if both Judkins and Sampson are active. item.title: Firing Mike Locksley Was Long Overdue — But Can Anyone Win at Maryland?

Maryland dismissed Mike Locksley on Wednesday after a 2-5 start and a 37-30 homecoming loss to Rutgers. The defeat extended the Terrapins’ Big Ten losing streak to 12 games. Aazaar Abdul-Rahim will serve as interim head coach . The change was overdue. Maryland had moved beyond a disappointing stretch into sustained regression. But firing Locksley cannot become an excuse for the university to avoid examining its own role. The Terrapins need a better coach. They also need an honest assessment of what it takes to compete in their conference. Otherwise, Wednesday simply starts the clock on the next dismissal. Maryland posted three consecutive winning seasons and won three straight bowl games from 2021 through 2023, a bowl-winning streak unprecedented in program history. Instead, Maryland brought him back. Now another season is being spent trying to identify where the rebuild should begin. Rutgers Cannot Be Explained Away by the Big Ten’s Heavyweights The conference provides a convenient explanation for Maryland’s struggles. There is truth in it. Building a contender in a league containing Ohio State, Michigan, Oregon, Penn State and other ambitious programs is an enormous assignment. But the Rutgers loss exposes the limits of that defense. A program seeking credibility has to win enough games against opponents closer to its competitive neighborhood. The Terrapins were not firing Locksley because he failed to deliver a national title. They were confronting a team that could no longer win a Big Ten game. Conference difficulty explains why the ceiling is hard to reach. It does not excuse a collapsing floor. Maryland’s Resource Problem Is Real Still, anyone presenting this as exclusively a coaching failure is leaving out an essential part of the story. When Maryland retained Locksley last November, athletic director Jim Smith also promised greater financial support. According to The Washington Post’s reporting at the time , Maryland’s football operating expenses were roughly $37 million in the financial data examined, compared with a Big Ten average above $58 million. Those were historical operating figures, not a verified comparison of current player-compensation budgets. Nevertheless, they illustrated a substantial gap. That matters when evaluating the next hire. A coach can improve evaluation, development, preparation and game management. He cannot personally eliminate every disadvantage in recruiting support, staffing, roster retention and institutional spending. Maryland needs to explain what has changed since Smith pledged additional resources — and how its next coach will be supported beyond the introductory news conference. Membership in a wealthy conference does not automatically make every member equally equipped to win. The Local Talent Argument Only Goes So Far Maryland should have recruiting advantages. Locksley’s own background illustrates the opportunity. A Washington, D.C., native with extensive regional connections, he built much of his reputation on recruiting. Maryland’s official biography credits him with signing numerous highly regarded prospects from the DMV during his career. But proximity is an opportunity, not ownership. The best local players can choose national programs. Maryland has to offer them a reason to stay, then develop and retain enough of them to build a complete roster. Signing a headline recruit is valuable. Constructing dependable offensive and defensive lines, maintaining depth and surviving injuries are what make a team competitive through a conference schedule. The next coach’s recruiting pitch must be supported by an organization capable of delivering on it. Can Anyone Really Win at Maryland? Yes — if winning means building a credible program that reaches bowls regularly, finishes with winning records and occasionally threatens the conference’s upper tier. Locksley’s own best seasons demonstrate that some version of that is achievable. If winning means routinely competing for Big Ten championships, the university has a much larger undertaking. Hiring a different personality will not be sufficient. Maryland does have tangible assets. Its Jones-Hill House facility includes an indoor football training space created from the former Cole Field House. The university has invested in the program’s physical infrastructure. The challenge is turning those assets into sustained competitiveness. That requires a coach with a clear football identity, a disciplined personnel strategy and institutional backing that lasts beyond one promising recruiting class. It also requires setting expectations that distinguish genuine progress from a convenient collection of nonconference victories. Maryland Needs More Than a New Name on the Door The next coach should be expected to improve the team. The Big Ten cannot become a permanent permission slip for losing. But Maryland’s administration should face expectations, too. What level of investment will it sustain? How will it support roster retention? What competitive standard will define success? How will it measure whether the program is actually closing the gap? Those questions belong alongside every discussion of coaching candidates. Locksley had enough time. His dismissal was warranted, and waiting longer would have been difficult to defend. Now Maryland must demonstrate that it understands the difference between replacing a coach and building a winning Big Ten program. item.title: Crystal Palace asked to retire Phoenix by animal rights group Peta
item.description: Crystal Palace asked to retire Phoenix by animal rights group Peta People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) has called on Crystal Palace to retire Phoenix, the club's American bald eagle mascot. In a letter addressed to chief executive Sharon Lacey, the animal rights group demanded that the club commit to never using a live animal mascot again. The practice of bringing a wild animal into a stadium environment is fundamentally flawed. Bald eagles are symbols of freedom that typically avoid close contact with humans, yet Phoenix is treated as a prop for entertainment. The combination of bright lights, loud noises, and boisterous crowds creates a setting where a bird can become frightened, disoriented, and panicked. The dangers are not theoretical. Peta pointed to incidents where eagles collided with glass windows and walls, and an owl died after being hit by a ball. One particularly alarming case involved a falcon that embedded its talons into a spectator's scalp. The risk extends to the animals as well, as seen in 2015 when a Charlton Athletic fan attempted to punch the former mascot, Kayla, during a League Cup tie. Crystal Palace already employs a human mascot to energise supporters. There is no justification for subjecting a wild animal to the stress of a matchday experience. While Phoenix was introduced in August 2024, the bird has not appeared at Selhurst Park since, and plans for a maiden flight across the pitch were reportedly abandoned. The club has failed to respond to Peta's letter or follow-up requests for comment. This silence is an inadequate response to the welfare and safety concerns raised.

item.title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026: 4 Matches That Could Soon Be Added to Card
item.description: WWE Crown Jewel will be back in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on November 7. The major Premium Live Event will feature two namesake title matches between the World Champions from RAW and SmackDown. On the men’s side, Sami Zayn will clash with Roman Reigns, while Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan will battle WWE titleholder Chelsea Green. As the road to Crown Jewel continues, we predict four more matches that could be added to the 2026 Crown Jewel card. WWE Women’s Tag Team Championships match On the October 16 episode of Friday Night SmackDown, Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley dethroned Lainey Reid and Fallon Henley to become the new WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions. Despite the setback, the dynamic duo of Fatal Influence is unlikely to sit back and watch. Instead, they might want to exact revenge and reclaim the titles. Therefore, this could set the tone for a huge rematch between both sides at the upcoming WWE Crown Jewel 2026 PLE. Jade Cargill vs. Charlotte Flair On the same episode of SmackDown, Charlotte Flair was originally supposed to team up with Tatum Paxley to challenge for the WWE Women’s Tag Team Championships. However, her heated rival, Jade Cargill, and her lackeys, Michin and B-Fab, ambushed her backstage. This ruled the Queen out of competing, and Alexa Bliss had to replace her. With Flair likely seeking payback from Cargill amid a months-long feud, they could clash at Crown Jewel 2026, possibly in a stipulation singles match. Je’Von Evans vs. Bron Breakker One of the most shocking moments at WWE Money in the Bank 2026 saw Je’Von Evans crash through an ambulance roof after Bron Breakker pushed him off the ladder. The two have been butting heads for a long time, and Evans even cost him a singles win over Penta. Should the Young OG heal up by Crown Jewel, this could lead to an exciting singles match between the dominant Breakker and the high-flying Evans. CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens CM Punk and Kevin Owens have shared one of the most heated rivalries in professional wrestling for years. Moreover, KO’s actions led to Punk losing the Undisputed WWE Title to Sami Zayn on SmackDown a few weeks ago. As tensions continue to escalate, WWE could book this marquee bout for a major event like WWE Crown Jewel 2026.

The Steelers announced the honor Wednesday after Ramsey played a key role in shutting down Tampa Bay's offense. Ramsey recorded 10 tackles, including nine solo stops, four tackles for loss and two sacks. He also played through a wrist injury that limited him in practice leading up to the game. item.description: New York Yankees owner Hal Steinbrenner New York Yankees owner Hal Steinbrenner met with the media on Wednesday and discussed what he thought went wrong in the postseason. While fans are blaming Aaron Boone and Brian Cashman for another season without a championship, Steinbrenner defended them. He made sure to let everyone know he thought the players were the reason the team failed. "(Boone) got us to the playoffs, and the bottom line is the players didn't live up to their end of the bargain in the playoffs," Steinbrenner told reporters on Wednesday . Specifically, Steinbrenner called out his position players for not putting up more runs. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! "I believe we absolutely had a team that was capable of winning a championship," Steinbrenner said on Wednesday . "I was disappointed, quite frankly, with the offense throughout the course of the year. As a whole, even though there were some bright spots, and (Ben) Rice had a great year, etc., as a whole they were very inconsistent when it came to run scoring. They were inconsistent for long periods of time." "That is certainly one part of the organization I'm going to be looking at from top to bottom," he added. "This is twice now that the offense has not come through." Against the Boston Red Sox, the offense scored 18 runs in two games. Against the Tampa Bay Rays, they managed just five runs across three games. As a whole, the offense scored the ninth-most runs in baseball and was tied for 11th in OPS. Steinbrenner also said that the pitching staff was the reason the team made the postseason, and he had nothing bad to say about them. To be fair, the Yankees were without Aaron Judge for most of the year, which obviously had a huge impact on the offense. item.title: Roger Goodell breaks silence on NFLPA asking for investigation into Jalen Hurts blood clot situation
item.description: Roger Goodell breaks silence on NFLPA asking for investigation into Jalen Hurts blood clot situation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the rest of the 2026 NFL season, as it was found that he has blood clots in his lungs, and he'll need to take blood thinners for treatment. It's a terrible situation for Hurts and the Eagles, but the circumstances of how things got to this point are a bit murky. Hurts played against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London with a blood clot in his calf, and after some still-undetermined amount of sleep. After the odd circumstances of Hurts' situation, the NFLPA asked for an investigation into the handling of Hurts' blood clot issue. The next day, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport shared how Roger Goodell broke his silence on this request for an investigation, and it was a simple three-word message from the NFL Commissioner. Roger Goodell breaks silence on NFLPA request for an investigation into Jalen Hurts situation "NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell says, 'We welcome it,' with regards to the NFLPA asking for an investigation on Jalen Hurts' medical situation," Rapoport shared. The NFLPA is asking for an investigation to get clarity on Hurts' situation, and the NFL, through the Commissioner, is welcoming it. This situation is far from over, as there's plenty more to figure out about what happened with Hurts following Week 4, when he was reportedly cleated, leading to the blood clot in his calf. What will make this investigation so interesting is that Hurts and his agent Nicole Lynn worked in cooperation with the Eagles' franchise to coordinate messaging after the fact. MORE : ESPN analyst proposes Eagles trade Saquon Barkley to Texans for very intriguing haul That would seem to imply that there isn't some contentious relationship between the Eagles and Hurts behind the scenes. Obviously it's not known one way or the other, but it seems apparent that Hurts and his team were on board with how things were handled; the story would look a bit different than it has so far. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell is welcoming an investigation request from the NFLPA, which is not a surprise. Considering the odd circumstances around this situation, it would've been surprising if the NFLPA didn't request an investigation. While it might be time before any results are found, if anything of note comes up, the NFL, the Eagles, and Hurts all seem to have no qualms about this situation. But for now, the NFLPA wants an investigation, and the NFL welcomes that, according to Goodell. item.title: Luka Doncic Sends Message to Lakers Fans Ahead of 1st Game of Season
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers All-Star point guard Luka Doncic took out a full page ad in the LA Times on Wednesday to send a message to fans ahead of their first game of the season against the Golden State Warriors. Doncic is one of the best players in the NBA, routinely securing All-NBA and All-Star selections, but one thing—perhaps the biggest thing—is missing from his resume: an NBA title. In his statement, he makes it clear what the Lakers’ goals are for this season. What Did Luka Doncic Say in the LA Times? “Dear LA,” Doncic wrote. “Tonight we start our run for the championship. “Every player dreams of holding that trophy. To do it for all of you amazing fans would mean everything to us. “Each of us understands what it means to put on this purple and gold jersey and follow the players who wore it before us. It means so much because of the passion and dedication that generations of you have all shown for this team. “I see it everywhere. The hats, the flags on cars, the murals. This city has people from mall over the world, speaking eery language, and the Lakers are the thing that brings everyone together. “We have a special team. We know what you expect, and we are going to do everything in our power to deliver it. “From the moment I arrived in LA, you welcomed me with open arms. That is something I will never forget. “So here is my promise to you: we are going to give you everything were have, every single night. No excuses. No nights off. “But we cannot do this alone. You are the best fans in the world, and we are going to need you. Every game, bring it with us. “Let’s go.” Oct 5, 2026; Sacramento, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts after a play dfirst quarter against the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center. Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images How Good is Luka Doncic? Doncic came to the Lakers midway through the 2024-25 season, headlining a massive three-team deal between the Lakers, the Dallas Mavericks and the Utah Jazz. He is the centerpiece of the Lakers’ roster, and proved he could be the best player on the team in his first full year on the squad. Doncic led the NBA in points per game last season with 33.5, and also logged 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists per game through 64 games. His time in LA thus far hasn’t been the best, suffering two early playoff exits in consecutive years, but Doncic and the Lakers will look to turn things around this season, which kicks off Wednesday at 7:00 p.m. PT against the Golden State Warriors. With less than a week to go before this year's Ballon d'Or ceremony in London, he's pushing hard to bolster his credentials for the prestigious award. The case in his favor is already compelling, yet for someone as driven and professional as Kane, there is always room to raise the bar further. Should he find the net on Wednesday against Arsenal — the club he represented as an eight-year-old — he will be on the verge of equaling a landmark record previously held by Cristiano Ronaldo. Erik ten Hag 'embarrassed' by Scott McTominay transfer as ex-Man United manager slams club bosses Cristiano Ronaldo delivers brutal Portugal 'ultimatum' after Jorge Jesus 'broke his word' -Credit:Naomi Baker, Getty Images The Portuguese icon remains the only player to have scored in 11 consecutive competitive matches, and Kane currently sits at nine. item.description: Last month’s Presidents Cup took me back. In 1979, after the U.S. had defeated Great Britain & Ireland in 14 of 15 matches from 1947 to 1977, the Ryder Cup enacted Jack Nicklaus’ suggestion that the GB&I side be expanded to include all of Europe. Europe won again in 1987 and retained the cup with a tie in 1989. For three straight sessions the Ryder Cup was theirs … unheard of. The change worked. For sure, it’s been a tougher climb for the Americans, but Nicklaus’ idea, supported by Lord Derby of the British PGA, resurrected the competition. By 1991, the “new” Ryder Cup, which critics, including the great English writer Peter Dobereiner, had declared dead with the expansion, had become arguably the keenest team event in sports. Which brings us back to the Presidents Cup. Acknowledging that international team events are forever a marriage of exhibition and competition, the Ryder Cup is now an exhibition, small e, and a Competition, capital C. You can’t be more than the captains from the inaugural 1994 match Fix A: No U.S. player may participate in both the Ryder Cup and the Presidents Cup within a designated two-year period (odd year followed by even year, beginning in 2027). I know what you might be thinking: There is an appetite for leveling the playing field, but that does not extend to threatening American victory in either competition. U.S. players would likely protest— With the prestige of our very country at stake, how can we pull punches? The PGA of America and its Ryder Cup players would suggest, as some did in 1979, that change would dilute their event. The PGA Tour would protest because, at first blush, such a change relegates the U.S. Presidents Cup team to second string, though that needn’t be (and the event itself is already there). Fix A might even make the U.S. team underdogs in the Presidents Cup, though based on World Ranking alone, that would be hard to accomplish. And would it be so bad if it did? What helps support the change, besides the wishes of a few tour wives and many TV ad salesmen, is a kind of fairness symmetry: No member of any of the three teams, U.S., Europe or International, would compete in more than one elite team competition during a two-event “cycle.” If Scottie Scheffler plays in the 2027 Ryder Cup, he may not play in the 2028 Presidents Cup. He may play in the 2029 Ryder Cup or in the 2030 Presidents Cup. He also could play in the 2031 Ryder Cup, which lies in the next designated two-year period. So, there are no extra reps for the Americans. In addition, audiences would see far more great American players. Good, no? Fix A also would force the U.S. to prove something it often espouses: that no tour is deeper, no group of players stronger, no competitive fiber tougher, than ours. How about this: We’re so good, we can field two teams. USA!!!! USA!!! Prohibiting U.S. players from playing in more than one team event every two-year cycle would be a radical alternative, but one that could make the Presidents Cup more competitive. Michael Reaves Guaranteed spots based on World Ranking could be sorted in different ways. It could be as rigid as assigning the “even” eligibility spots to one cup and the odds to the other. But given the ever-changing World Ranking, and the choices players make about the matches they choose to play, plus the strength of different players on different golf courses (home v. away, potential pairings, etc.) it would probably come down to the two American captains working it out. Which, for better or worse, adds a whole new level of drama to the process. (Kind of like the recent proposal that the MLB allow higher seeds to choose their opponents in the playoffs.) Clearly this idea makes things more challenging for both U.S teams, and far more complicated for U.S. captains. You may say, “Why should the Americans have to be the ones to change?!!” Because we can afford to. But on to the next option. Fix B: No U.S. captain’s pick shall play in more than one international team event in the designated two-year period (odd year followed by even year). Instead of 12, only six Americans are restricted from playing in two international team competitions within a given two-year period. In a world of two-tier stardom, Tier 1 continues to appear in both events. Fix C: A maximum of eight U.S. players may compete in two team events within a designated two-year period. The top tier gets deeper, and the limitations on the U.S. teams lessen. I think all three of these fixes have merit and could help make the Presidents Cup a stronger competition, although Fix A won’t get off the first tee, I’m sure. (The irony is that the biggest complainant will be the PGA Tour, whose event has the most to gain.) So let’s go with Fix B, beginning with the 2027 Ryder Cup. Only six members of one U.S. team may repeat on the other. Still tougher for the Americans, but so was the addition of Europe to the GB&I side in1979. And the potential for making the Presidents Cup competition a real competition is strong. J.J. Spaun just called. He likes ’em all.

item.title: Suwarso: Como hosting Manchester United ‘is unreal, like a gift’ for club
item.description: Suwarso: Como hosting Manchester United ‘is unreal, like a gift’ for club Como President Mirwan Suwarso admits hosting Manchester United in the Champions League is ‘unreal’ for a club that was in the third division until 2021. ‘It is like a gift.’ It kicks off at the Stadio Sinigaglia at 17.45 UK time (18.45 CEST). You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Inter vs. Shakhtar Donetsk on the Liveblog. ITALY – SEPTEMBER 10: General view inside the stadium before the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Como 1907 and RB Leipzig at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on September 10, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) This is another prestigious opportunity for the club, who host former Treble winners Manchester United in their third ever Champions League fixture. They beat RB Leipzig here 4-1, then were narrowly beaten 3-2 away to Feyenoord after fumbling the lead. Suwarso took Como to Champions League BOLOGNA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 01: Mirwan Suwarso president of Como during the Serie A match between Bologna and Como at Stadio Renato Dall’Ara on February 01, 2025 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) “We welcomed them with English weather,” smiled Suwarso to Sky Sport Italia under an umbrella in the pouring rain by Lake Como. “This situation is very strange for me, and it’s not right for a club like Como. This is something like a gift we are trying to do it and take it one day at a time, but this is not where we thought we would ever be. It’s unreal.” Como were in Serie B as recently as the 2023/24 season, and in Serie C just a couple of years before that, a club that went bankrupt three times in 15 years. Indonesian businessman Suwarso and his family took charge and rebuilt them from the ground up, aided by coach and previously player Cesc Fabregas. ITALY – MAY 02: SSC Como 1907 coach Cesc Fabregas looks on during the Serie A match between Como 1907 and SSC Napoli at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on May 02, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Considering so many investors rush to the Premier League, why are some now drawn to Serie A? “This was not something we intended to do at the beginning, but it was an opportunity that presented itself. We feel a responsibility to the city that entrusted us, now we just have to trust that respect and do our best to make them proud.” Jesus Rodriguez sustained a serious injury in training and is expected to be out of action for circa two months, with Moise Kean, Assane Diao and Trevoh Chalobah already on the absentee list. It has prompted them to remove Jesus Rodriguez from the UEFA squad list, replacing him with midfielder Maxence Caqueret.

Rose comments on Milan ahead of Europa League clash BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 18: Marco Rose, Manager of Bournemouth, celebrates at full-time following the Premier League 2026/27 match between AFC Bournemouth and Sunderland at Vitality Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) There is no denying that a visit from Milan is an enormous occasion for Bournemouth, who had been on the brink of collapse after being handed a -17 point deduction while in League Two in 2008-09. Still, Rose believes that the crucial games while in League Two were bigger occasions than the upcoming visit of Milan. “It’s a huge game. It’s a big game and we are looking forward to play it, but I think many years ago the club had a much bigger game after the point reduction and they needed to win the last game at home and Fletch scored a goal. Always, but it’s not about Fletch, it’s about the whole team,” said Rose during his pre-match press conference on Wednesday. (via Bournemouth Echo ) “So this is a foundation to be here, to have this kind of games, and we are looking forward to play this game. A huge club of Europe is coming here, but we feel prepared. We love to play this kind of games and now, yeah, we’re going to go for it tomorrow.” BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 15: Alvaro Rodriguez of Bournemouth celebrates scoring his team’s third goal with teammates during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between AFC Bournemouth and SK Sturm Graz at Bournemouth Stadium on October 15, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images) Despite this game being an unimaginable fixture 15 years ago, Rose believes he has the squad ready to challenge any side in the Premier League and Europa League. “Well, my feeling is we can compete with everyone in this league, we can compete with everyone in the Premier League. Some players getting back: Justin is back, Amin is back, Junior’s on a good way. “If we have our whole squad, if we have competition into the squad, if we can use the squad because of the many games we have, then I feel us in a quite good spot to compete everywhere.” This will not be the first time that Rose has gone up against Milan head coach Amorim, though. ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, reacts during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Atalanta BC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 18, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) He recalled: “I faced him in the Champions League when he was coach with Sporting. And yeah, it’s a good coach, top coach. And if you see AC Milan now, if you analyse them, you see a clear coaching style. A really good side. Individual quality, clear plan, good in pressing, good in counter-pressing. “So things everyone missed maybe a little bit here during the time with Man United, but now another group, another energy. It’s a tough, tough opponent we face tomorrow. This will be Rose’s first time facing Milan, though. “Yeah, I played two times Inter Milan, but never AC Milan. I just had a talk with Duncan, our kit man, and we spoke about the Dutch group in AC Milan, the big time in the ’80s. Yeah, this kind of guys. So again, it’s a huge club with a lot of titles, international titles as well, Champions League. So it’s just good to have them here. “And I love Luka Modrić as a player, as a person. I admire him. I have a deep respect for his career and looking forward to meet him tomorrow again, because we know each other from games against Real Madrid, and looking forward to see him. ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Luka Modric of AC Milan is challenged by Charles De Ketelaere of Atalanta BC during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Atalanta BC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 18, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) “The quality of the opponent is really, really good, really tough to play in everything, out and in possession. So it’s getting a tough game. And if we are involved, we know we want to play our intensity. We want to play forward, we want to be front-footed. Nothing changed. So it can be quite interesting, yeah.” Rose was asked if he thinks Milan will be Bournemouth’s toughest opponents in the league phase, to which he responded: “Well, yeah, Sociedad away was tough as well, and sometimes the smaller games are much, much more difficult to play. So every game, every opponent is interesting, and tomorrow’s AC Milan, that’s what we are focused on.

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
